issue_context.title: API: rename DataFrame.applymap -> DataFrame.map
issue_context.body:
I propose deprecating `DataFrame.applymap` and move its functionality to a new `DataFrame.map` method. The name `map` will better communicate that this is the `DataFrame` equivalent of `Series.map`. The current name can IMO be a bit confusing because the name contains both `"apply"` and `"map"`, while just having `"map"` is clearer IMO.
 
See a discussion on this [here](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/52140#issuecomment-1482789939).

CC @rhshadrach

review_comments:
This is really an aside, but I wanted to mention as we do have the opportunity here. In the cases where we're passing through kwargs to a user-passed function, I have increasingly become a fan of having `kwargs` be a normal argument as opposed to `**kwargs`. While these points are relatively minor, the benefit is:

 - No possibility of name conflicts between the pandas method and the user passed function (e.g. `func` can't have an argument `na_action` here)
 - Typos (e.g. `df.map(n_action='ignore')`) generate better error messages

One possible downside is users have to do `df.map(foo, kwargs={'a': 1})` instead of `df.map(foo, a=1)` but I personally don't think that as much of a downside.

I agree with all your points personally and I try not to use `*args` or `**kwargs` at all. Also, if you look at e.g. numpy, it uses  `*args` or `**kwargs` alot, and I think it makes numpy harder to use than it needs to.

OTOH, there is social expectations and people are used to  `*args` or `**kwargs`, so i don't know, could be a too big change now that we already have selected the  `*args` or `**kwargs` route.

There is though also [ParamSpec](https://peps.python.org/pep-0612/), which we could implement to partly alleviate this problem.
